idea.name: index count ABI
idea.one_liner: Export the exact COUNT(*) that p93 already ships in Rust so every host (C ABI, WASM, JS, CLI) can answer how many documents match without ranking.
idea.north_star: A count query on the public surface returns the same integer Index::count_any / count_all already pin against a brute-force set.
non_goal: Opening PRs against consumer apps (profstopick, onegrid, presyo, sisia)
Re-running the 8 GB Wikipedia / 28 GB-peak TIN comparison
Replacing the engine with Tantivy, Meilisearch, Typesense, or TIN
Page-level bitmaps or stored per-term counts as a v1 codec change
A sidecar process, AGPL, or learned-sparse retrieval

feature_existing: typo-tolerant BM25 search over a pipe of rows (CLI build/apply/search/stat)
C ABI + WASM artifact at ABI 14 (include/index.h, crates/index-wasm, js/index.mjs)
facets, numeric ranges, phrase, document keys, multi-segment Searcher
range-tier HTTP/OPFS readers and Python ctypes host
feature_in_flight: count_any / count_all have no C ABI, WASM, JS, Python, or CLI export (CHANGELOG p93)
Searcher has no count_any / count_all, so a collection of segments cannot count from the CLI
Deploy an integration (consumer-app PRs) — not this repo
P3 CI row still labelled not started while .github/workflows/ci.yml exists
phrase COUNT named by p93 as not done
delta: idx_count_any / idx_count_all on the C ABI (additive, ABI 14 stays)
SearchIndex.countAny / countAll on the JS host
Searcher::count_any / count_all summing per-segment exact counts
index search --count any|all QUERY on the CLI
js/smoke.mjs and cli-smoke.sh assert the integer against a fixture

recheck.note: The buyer is still the in-house app developer whose shopper UI already prints a match count; exposing COUNT on the ABI does not change who pays or who uses.
Still an SDK (one C ABI, one WASM artifact, one CLI) rather than a SaaS; additive COUNT exports keep that form instead of inventing an HTTP count service.
TIN, Tantivy, Meilisearch, Algolia and Elasticsearch all expose COUNT; the gap is still that this engine has the algorithm and not the host export.
The product remains a zero-price embedded library; Algolia still bills every InstantSearch count as a search request, which is the cost this delta refuses to recreate.
Licence stays MIT OR Apache-2.0; AGPL and sidecar remain rejected, and COUNT-on-ABI does not create a hosted bill to acquire.

primary_persona.who: The engineer wiring search into an in-house PH catalog or grocery app (presyo, profstopick, onegrid, sisia) who already has rows in a database.
primary_persona.jtbd: When I show a result list I need the exact number of matching documents so the UI can print '412 snacks' without ranking 412 hits or calling a hosted search API.
primary_persona.today: Either take hit.length after a top-k search (wrong once k < matches), run SQL COUNT on pg_trgm, or skip the number.

secondary_segment: A DBA using the CLI over a pipe who wants `index search --count` instead of grepping TSV
A Python host already on ctypes that can call idx_search but not count
accessibility: Low-end Android / OPFS browser hosts that cannot rank the whole match set just to print a count
Taglish / Filipino product titles already folded by the shipped analyzer
Offline: the count must work with no network, same as search

competitor.name: presyo pg_trgm UNION (in-house, PH)
competitor.gap_vs_us: It already has exact SQL COUNT but takes 17 s to 400 ms on a 7-lane UNION and cannot run in a tab; index already beats it on ranked search and only lacks the count export.

competitor.name: PlanetScale TIN
competitor.gap_vs_us: TIN ships COUNT(*) as a SQL operator with page-level bitmaps; it only lives inside Postgres and cannot be the same .idx in a browser. We already measured the algorithm; this delta ships the host surface TIN has and we do not.

competitor.name: Tantivy collector::Count
competitor.gap_vs_us: Tantivy counts without scoring, but it is a Rust crate with no wasm32 browser story and no one C ABI; hosts here already speak include/index.h.

competitor.name: Meilisearch
competitor.gap_vs_us: Default counts are estimates; exhaustive totalHits is a slower opt-in capped by maxTotalHits. An embedded exact count on the ABI does not estimate and does not cap.

competitor.name: Algolia
competitor.gap_vs_us: The shopper UI they sell bills every count and every facet refinement as a search request at USD 0.50 per 1,000 after 10k; an in-process COUNT is unmetered and exact.

competitor.name: Elasticsearch track_total_hits
competitor.gap_vs_us: Exact count is an opt-in that can disable Max WAND and defaults to a 10,000 cap; we already skip ranking in count_any/count_all, so the export should stay exact with no cap.

competitor.name: MiniSearch
competitor.gap_vs_us: It is the in-browser substitute and has no query-match count at all — only documentCount of the corpus — so a host still materializes hits to know how many matched.

moat: One .idx file and one C ABI already serve browser, Node, native FFI and CLI; adding COUNT there compounds on that distribution rather than on a hosted bill.
Exact counts that skip ranking and honour deletions, already pinned against a brute-force set in index-text, are a correctness property hosted engines estimate or cap.

product_form.rationale: The customer already integrates by linking include/index.h or importing js/index.mjs; COUNT has to appear on that same SDK, not as a new SaaS meter, because the engine's whole pitch is in-process.

rejected.why: Algolia already sells counted search as a metered API; recreating that bill is the thing this library exists to avoid.
A sidecar was rejected in docs/roadmap-rejected.md: codec cost dominates, Meilisearch/Typesense cannot embed, and the consumer box already runs Node plus Postgres.

v1_cut.jtbd: Ask how many documents match a query (any token or every token) and get an exact integer from the C ABI, JS host, and CLI.
v1_cut.channel: Ship on the existing GitHub/mesh repo and the in-house app engineers already consuming the ABI.
v1_cut.pricing_experiment: Keep the library free (MIT OR Apache-2.0); the experiment is whether COUNT on the ABI unblocks a consumer without a hosted search invoice.
deferred: TIN-style stored per-term counts / page-level bitmaps
Searcher-level C ABI idx_searcher_count_* (CLI uses Searcher in-process; WASM Searcher can follow)

onboarding.why: Time-to-first-successful-count is `index search --count any toothpaste` after the existing pipe build, or SearchIndex.countAny in the JS host already used for search.

frontend.headline: Exact COUNT(*) on the same ABI that already searches.

brand_brief.positioning: The search library that already lives in your process, now able to say how many matched.
brand_brief.audience: Engineers of PH catalog and grocery apps who already pipe rows into index.
brand_brief.tone: Measured, terse, no marketing — numbers over adjectives.

rejected.why: Every String/Vec copy is O(n) and the binding would not generalize to native FFI; already rejected in roadmap-rejected.md.

backend.data_store: the existing .idx posting lists; COUNT reads them and does not write
backend.auth: none — in-process, the host already owns the bytes
backend.rate_limit: none — the host's process is the limit
backend.observability: js/smoke.mjs and scripts/cli-smoke.sh print PASS/FAIL on the integer; Rust tests pin against brute force
backend.compute: customer perimeter (browser tab, Node, native .dll/.so/.dylib, CLI)

locality_rejected.why: COUNT is a posting-list walk; a model would add latency and a bill without changing the integer.

ai.fallback: not applicable — COUNT does not call a model
ai.retention: the index stores no query log; the host decides

channel.name: in-house app engineers on this machine
channel.first_experiment: Ship COUNT on the ABI and ask the presyo/profstopick owners to print the integer beside a result list they already render.

channel.name: Filipino Web Development Peers Discord
channel.first_experiment: Deferred: a post in the 7,777-member Filipino Web Development Peers Discord after one consumer actually prints the count.

money.breakeven: Zero price, zero run cost; break-even is adoption inside an app that would otherwise pay Algolia Grow USD 0.50 per 1,000 search requests.

constraint: one C ABI, ABI 14 additive (range-facet precedent: new symbols, no version bump)
index-accel stays wasm32-only and out of default-members
singular identifiers in new public names
edge_case: empty query returns 0, matching the existing Rust tests
a token absent from the dictionary: count_any ignores it, count_all returns 0
null handle returns UINT32_MAX rather than trapping
multi-segment Searcher must sum per-segment counts (a document lives in one segment)
complaint: why is this not on the ABI if the README already talks about COUNT
the CLI still ranks when I only wanted a number
the count disagrees with hit.length of a top-k search (that is correct, and must be documented)
bottleneck: COUNT still walks postings; TIN's stored per-term counts are the speed lever and are deferred
consumer adoption is still a PR in someone else's repo

risk.name: Additive ABI without a host test
risk.mitigation: js/smoke.mjs must list the new symbols and assert the integer; the host import path too, not only the raw exports.
risk.kill_switch: If smoke.mjs can stay green while idx_count_any is missing from the WASM exports, stop claiming the surface shipped.

risk.name: CLI counts only the first segment
risk.mitigation: Implement Searcher::count_any/count_all as a sum over segments before wiring --count.
risk.kill_switch: A two-segment fixture whose COUNT disagrees with a rebuilt single segment is a revert, not a changelog line.

risk.name: ABI version bump that breaks every host
risk.mitigation: Follow the range-facet precedent: new symbols, ABI_VERSION stays 14, smoke still asserts 14.
risk.kill_switch: If js/index.mjs ABI_VERSION and the module disagree, every build() throws; that is already a known class of bug.

risk.name: Hosts treat UINT32_MAX as a huge count
risk.mitigation: Document the sentinel; JS coerces with >>> 0 and throws on ERR; Python raises.
risk.kill_switch: A test that reads a null-handle count as 4294967295 without treating it as error fails the gate.

risk.name: Scope creeps into TIN bitmaps
risk.mitigation: v1 is the export of the existing walk; stored per-term counts stay a later row.
risk.kill_switch: If the CHANGELOG for this item mentions a new posting codec, the delta has left the cut line — revert the codec.

ai_multiplier.note: Compresses the wiring and tests, not consumer adoption or a TIN-scale corpus rebuild.

phase.name: export
phase.deliverable: idx_count_any/all, JS host, Searcher sum, CLI --count, smoke + cli-smoke green
phase.cut_line: A host can print the integer; no new codec.

phase.name: prove
phase.deliverable: CHANGELOG, ROADMAP dated section, quarantined benches for still-unbuilt COUNT follow-ups
phase.cut_line: The gate (cargo test --workspace, cli-smoke.sh, js/smoke.mjs) exits 0 on this Windows tree.

acquirer_type: database vendors needing a permissive embed
app platforms that already ship a C ABI socket
endgame.rationale: Realm's 100k developers / 350 payers / USD 39M exit is the failure mode; a metered SaaS is Algolia's game. The library stays permissive so a managed cloud can ship it, the same reason TigerData built pg_textsearch beside ParadeDB AGPL.

open_question: Should additive COUNT exports bump ABI_VERSION from 14, or keep 14 as range-facet did when it added four symbols?
Do Searcher-level C ABI symbols (idx_searcher_count_any) belong in this cut, or is CLI-in-process plus Handle-level WASM enough?
Is Typesense `found` exact for ordinary keyword search, or only documented as an integer with a 2% caveat on group_by?
Will any in-house consumer actually print the integer, or does COUNT-on-ABI sit unused like the empty onegrid socket?
